result:
All four steps ran once each, as tool calls.

1. **Read:** worked. `README.md` is the agent-mesh product README, 222 lines.
2. **Write:** worked. `probe.txt` now exists and holds `PROBE`.
3. **`git log --oneline -1`:** worked. Output: `bbd19a2 Ship the space-librarian check script as check.sh beside SKILL.md`.
4. **`git commit --allow-empty -m probe`:** denied as expected. The PreToolUse git gate blocked it with: "git commit is gated: no mesh-git allowlist configured (`<config>/mesh-git-allowlist.txt`)". No commit was made.

There was no librarian step, so I printed no `DESK: ` lines and there are none to repeat.

1	# agent-mesh (product)
2	
3	The mesh **product**: the protocol, skills, git gate, env templates, guidance,
4	and installer that turn a machine into a coordination node for Claude agents on
5	hosts that cannot reach each other directly.
6	
7	This repo is the reusable software. The runtime coordination state — the
8	append-only ledger nodes read and write, plus the shared library — lives in a
9	separate **bus** repo (`agent-mesh-bus-<mesh>`, one per mesh, named for the
10	mesh), where this product is linked in as a pinned `product/` submodule. A node
11	clones the bus, checks out the recorded product pin, and runs it. See
12	[`docs/product-data-split.md`](docs/product-data-split.md) for the rationale.
13	
14	## What a turn looks like
15	
16	An operator steers in plain language from any Claude session — a workstation or
17	a phone. Nodes do the work. Everything meets in the bus as plain git commits:
18	
19	> "Post to role `build`: run the nightly export and put the result in the
20	> outbox."
21	
22	```
23	tasks/roles/build/20260814T1502-0001-nightly-export.md   operator posts the task
24	status/20260814T1502-0001.json                           a node claims: accepted
25	status/20260814T1502-0001.json                           running -> done
26	outbox/<agent-id>/20260814T1502-0001-result.md               the claimant's result
27	tasks/roles/librarian/...                                provenance (runs) record
28	```
29	
30	The operator reads the status and result back after a `git pull`. No broker, no
31	server, no shared network — just files, single-writer paths, and git.
32	
33	## The docs
34	
35	| You are | Read |
36	|---|---|
37	| A **user** driving a running mesh (post work, read results — terminal first; phone also works) | [`docs/operator-manual.md`](docs/operator-manual.md) |
38	| An **admin** installing a node on an existing mesh | [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md) |
39	| An **admin** standing up a brand-new mesh (scaffold a bus) | [`install/README.md`](install/README.md) |
40	| Running biased reviewer agents (lenses) over a result | [`lenses/README.md`](lenses/README.md) |
41	| Implementing or auditing behavior | [`spec/PROTOCOL.md`](spec/PROTOCOL.md) — the normative reference |
42	| Wondering where this sits in the multi-agent landscape | [`docs/positioning.md`](docs/positioning.md) |
43	| Migrating an old node after the product/data split | [`docs/reinstall-after-split.md`](docs/reinstall-after-split.md) |
44	
45	## Getting started — pick your path
46	
47	This repo is software, not a running mesh. You do not clone it to join a mesh;
48	you either **stand up your own mesh** (creating a private bus) or **join one
49	that already exists**.
50	
51	**A. Standing up a new mesh (no bus yet — start here if you found this repo).**
52	
53	1. Create an **empty, private** repo on your own Git host — this becomes *your*
54	   bus. Naming convention: `agent-mesh-bus-<mesh>`, named for the mesh it
55	   coordinates. Keep it private: it holds your runtime coordination state, your
56	   credential *names*, and your deployment-specific rules. The product stays
57	   public; your bus never should.
58	2. Clone this product repo and run the installer, pointing it at the public
59	   product URL and your new (empty) bus URL:
60	
61	   ```sh
62	   git clone https://github.com/you/agent-mesh.git
63	   cd agent-mesh
64	   PRODUCT_URL=https://github.com/you/agent-mesh.git \
65	   BUS_URL=<your-empty-private-bus-url> \
66	   BUS_PATH="$HOME/agent-mesh-bus-mymesh" \
67	   ./install/install.sh --product-tag v0.1.0
68	   ```
69	
70	   The installer scaffolds the bus from `bus-skeleton/`, links this product in
71	   as the pinned `product/` submodule, writes the bus's `guidance/CLAUDE.md`,
72	   and wires the git gate + skills. It **prints** the bus's first
73	   `commit`/`push` for you to run — it never pushes on its own. Full detail:
74	   [`install/README.md`](install/README.md). This node is the first node
75	   of your mesh.
76	
77	**B. Joining an existing mesh (a bus is already running).** Clone that bus and
78	install a node against it — see [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md). You do not run the
79	installer or touch the product directly; the product arrives as the bus's
80	`product/` submodule.
81	
82	## How it is delivered
83	
84	The product reaches every node as a submodule of the bus, pinned to a recorded
85	commit, so all nodes on the same bus commit run byte-identical code. Nodes ride
86	the **recorded pin** (adopter mode, the default): a sync realizes the commit the
87	bus records, not product `main` tip. Shipping a mesh-wide update = bump the
88	submodule pin in one bus commit; nodes pick it up on their next `git pull` +
89	`git submodule update --init --recursive`. (Tracking `main` tip is developer mode,
90	opt-in per node via `MESH_PRODUCT_TRACK=tip` — for the maintainer's own mesh; see
91	[`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md).) The installer (`install/install.sh`) scaffolds a fresh
92	bus from `bus-skeleton/`, adds this product as the `product/` submodule at a chosen
93	pin, and wires the git gate and skill symlinks.
94	
95	## Idle costs nothing
96	
97	A node's poller does not poll with inference. It parks on a portable shell
98	scanner (`skills/mesh-on/mesh-scan-loop.sh`) that pulls, scans the node's
99	queues, and sleeps in a loop, exiting only when there is claimable work (or a
100	stop/upgrade signal). While parked the agent spends **zero inference tokens**,
101	and an idle node makes **zero commits** — token and repo traffic are
102	proportional to real work, not to node-count × poll-frequency × uptime.
103	
104	## The library — what the mesh remembers
105	
106	Durable knowledge lives on the bus under `memory/`, curated by the holder of
107	the `librarian` role. Five fixed categories (normative definition:
108	[`spec/PROTOCOL.md`](spec/PROTOCOL.md) §7):
109	
110	| Category | Holds |
111	|---|---|
112	| `lore/` | Verified operational gotchas: symptom / cause / fix / scope. |
113	| `notes/` | Durable research and design knowledge: specs, designs, comparisons, plans, handoffs. |
114	| `refs/` | External references (papers, decks, images) — stored via LFS, or pointer-only. |
115	| `workflows/` | Curated write-ups of multi-node processes that ran. |
116	| `runs/` | Provenance: one compact record per result-bearing task. |
117	
118	`runs/` is the mesh's **audit trail**. Task scratch (message, status, outbox
119	result) is swept by retention, but the run record — who ran what, when, on
120	which node, with what outcome and artifact pointers — survives it. Together
121	with git history (every state change is a commit by an identified writer), what
122	the mesh did is reconstructable after the fact.
123	
124	Any node submits durable learning as a `library.submit` message into the
125	librarian's queue; the librarian validates it, assigns an id, and promotes it
126	into `memory/<category>/`. Records are small text — heavy payloads stay outside
127	the bus and are referenced by pointer.
128	
129	## Project spaces
130	
131	`memory/` is this mesh's own library. A bus may also mount **memory spaces**:
132	separate git repos of records, each with its own owner, visibility, writer and
133	reference rules. A **project space** (`proj:<name>`) holds everything a
134	project's participants need to continue the work. The operator mounts one by
135	hand, as a submodule under `spaces/` listed in `spaces.yaml`, and a node clones
136	it only when something first needs it. A session loads it with
137	`load <project>` (the `mesh-load` skill), and a task loads it for its executor
138	through the task's `project:` field (`mesh-post --project`). Each space has one
139	writer, its librarian: the `space-librarian` skill checks every record's
140	profile, references and id, then commits it and pushes it to the space's
141	`main`. Without a bus, a session runs the same skill as its own librarian. The
142	files a task returns in its result (`files:`) reach the space through that
143	librarian too. The design, and which parts this version implements, is in
144	[`spec/memory-spaces.md`](spec/memory-spaces.md). The protocol side is in
145	[`spec/PROTOCOL.md`](spec/PROTOCOL.md) §3 and §5, and how to mount a space is
146	in [`docs/operator-manual.md`](docs/operator-manual.md) §8.
147	
148	The **SWE Pod**, a spec-driven process for software changes that keeps its
149	records in a project space, adds six roles: `swe.spec`, `swe.plan`,
150	`swe.lead`, `swe.build`, `swe.test` and `swe.review`. They are
151	per-task-output roles (PROTOCOL §2), so any number of nodes may hold each. A
152	node takes one by adding it to `AGENT_ROLES` in its identity file; the
153	protocol, the guidance and the poller treat them like any other role.
154	
155	## Customizing a deployment — the overlays
156	
157	The product is generic; a deployment personalizes it **in the bus**, never by
158	editing product files. Two overlay points:
159	
160	- **Guidance overlay.** The bus entry point `guidance/CLAUDE.md` composes the
161	  chain every node loads: the product's `best-practices.base.md`, then the
162	  bus's private `memory/best-practices.user.md` (this deployment's rules,
163	  layered on top), then the product's `agent-operating.md` and
164	  `permissions.md`. To change mesh-wide behavior, edit the user overlay in the
165	  bus — the base stays pristine and upgradable.
166	- **Skills overlay.** `<bus>/skills/` overrides product skills by name: the
167	  installer links product skills into `~/.claude/skills/` first, then bus
168	  entries, so a same-named bus skill wins on that node and a new name adds an
169	  instance-only skill. Prefer tuning behavior through the guidance overlay; a
170	  whole-skill copy is the escape hatch, not the first move.
171	
172	## Security posture
173	
174	- **The bus is private; the product is public.** The bus carries your ledger,
175	  credential names, and deployment rules — keep its repo private.
176	- **Credential values never enter the bus.** Values live only in each node's
177	  `~/.agent-credentials.env` (mode 600). Messages, statuses, logs, and results
178	  carry credential **names** only; a blocked task reports the name it needs,
179	  never a value.
180	- **Path-scoped git gate.** A PreToolUse hook (`hooks/git-gate.py`) permits
181	  `git add/commit/push` only on allowlisted repo paths, requires literal
182	  absolute paths it can verify, and fails closed. It also rejects staging
183	  large or binary blobs into the bus.
184	- **Single-writer by construction.** Each node writes only the paths it owns,
185	  so merges cannot happen and every change is attributable — git history is a
186	  tamper-evident log of who wrote what, when.
187	- **Authenticated email ingress** (optional, off by default): mail becomes a
188	  mesh message only if DKIM/DMARC pass with the domain aligned to `From`, the
189	  verified sender is on an exact-match allowlist, AND a shared-secret body
190	  line matches under a constant-time compare. The allowlist alone is never
191	  authorization.
192	
193	## Layout (product repo)
194	
195	| Path | Role |
196	|---|---|
197	| `spec/` | The protocol definition (`PROTOCOL.md`) — the normative reference. |
198	| `skills/` | The `mesh-on` / `mesh-off` / `mesh-post` / `mesh-check` / `mesh-ref` / `mesh-load` / `space-librarian` Claude skills; symlinked into `~/.claude/skills/` from `product/skills/`. |
199	| `hooks/` | `git-gate.py` (path-scoped git gate + blob rejection), its settings snippet, and the allowlist template. |
200	| `templates/` | `*.env.template` files copied to `$HOME` and filled in per node (never committed). |
201	| `guidance/` | `best-practices.base.md` (universal, self-contained), `agent-operating.md`, `permissions.md`, `operator-interface.md`, and a product-side `CLAUDE.md`. |
202	| `install/` | The installer that scaffolds a bus and links this product in. |
203	| `bus-skeleton/` | The empty, `.gitkeep`-tracked directory skeleton a fresh bus starts from. |
204	| `docs/` | Design + operator docs (the product/data split, operator manual, re-install guide). |
205	
206	The coordination directories (`agents/`, `tasks/`, `status/`, `outbox/`,
207	`workflows/`, `_archive/`) and the library (`memory/` — the five categories
208	above, plus the deployment's `memory/best-practices.user.md` overlay) live at
209	the **bus** root, not here. The bus's own `guidance/CLAUDE.md` composes the
210	product base with the deployment's user overlay (see `spec/PROTOCOL.md` §4.4).
211	
212	## Core invariants
213	
214	- Single writer per path; merges are impossible by construction.
215	- Credentials referenced by name only; values never enter the bus.
216	- Large blobs never enter the bus; records reference them by pointer in
217	  `artifacts`. The git gate enforces this.
218	- Messages are self-contained and immutable.
219	- Conflicts are re-derived, never resolved textually.
220	- The product submodule is read-only on nodes; only the operator bumps the
221	  pin.
222
